source_user: Calculation case 155: a model has 56 layers, 6 KV heads, head dimension 96, sequence length 1024, and BF16/FP16 KV values. Estimate bytes for one request's K/V cache. Show the formula and report GiB.
source_assistant: Use 2 × layers × sequence_length × KV_heads × head_dim × bytes_per_value. Here this is 2 × 56 × 1024 × 6 × 96 × 2 = 132120576 bytes = 0.123047 GiB. This excludes allocator metadata and other runtime memory.
corrected_answer:
Assumptions: dense (non-MLA) transformer using GQA with 6 KV head(s) shared across the query heads; K and V materialized separately; BF16/FP16 KV elements at 2 byte(s) per element; exactly one sequence of 1024 tokens fully cached (prefill complete, no eviction); no paged-block padding, no quantization scales, no allocator or fragmentation overhead included.

Formula: bytes = 2 (one K tensor + one V tensor) x layers x sequence_length x kv_heads x head_dim x bytes_per_element.

Substitution: 2 x 56 x 1024 x 6 x 96 x 2 = 132120576 bytes = 126.000 MiB = 0.123047 GiB.

Mechanism: each decode step appends one K and one V vector of width kv_heads x head_dim per layer, so KV grows strictly linearly in sequence length and is the dominant per-request memory term at long context; weights are per-model and amortized across concurrency, KV is not.

Boundary conditions and falsifiable predictions:
- Under PagedAttention (vLLM) the allocation is quantized to blocks (typically 16 or 32 tokens), so measured occupancy is ceil(1024/block)*block tokens worth of KV, never less than the number above.
- Under tensor parallelism TP, per-GPU KV is total/TP only when 6 % TP == 0. With TP > 6 the runtime must replicate KV heads, so aggregate KV across GPUs exceeds 132120576 bytes; this is directly testable by comparing reported free KV blocks at TP=6 versus TP=2*6.
- MLA / cross-layer KV sharing / sliding-window or chunked attention invalidate this formula and would make it an over-estimate.
- Speculative decoding, beam search, or n>1 sampling multiply live KV by the number of concurrent branches.
- Quantizing KV to FP8/INT8 halves this figure but adds scale tensors and can change accuracy; validate on your eval set before relying on the smaller footprint.
- Peak resident memory is higher than steady state during prefill because of attention workspace and the logits buffer.

Serving-capacity use: usable KV bytes = total_HBM - weights - activation/workspace - CUDA context and fragmentation headroom (budget 5-10%). Dividing that by the per-request figure above gives an upper bound on concurrency, not an achievable one, because request lengths are skewed.

Evidence required to confirm: model config.json (num_hidden_layers, num_key_value_heads, head_dim or hidden_size/num_attention_heads, and any MLA/kv-sharing fields); the serving engine's KV dtype and block size; engine startup log of total KV cache blocks; and nvidia-smi / torch.cuda.memory_summary() before and after loading one request of exactly 1024 tokens.

Rollback threshold: if measured KV per request exceeds this estimate by more than 15% at the target context length, or free KV blocks fall below 10% at target concurrency, stop the rollout and re-derive from the actual engine config rather than raising max_num_seqs.
risks: Source answer states the formula and correct arithmetic but omits all assumptions (GQA, no MLA, no paged padding), so it can be misapplied to MLA models.
No mention of PagedAttention block rounding, so capacity plans built on this number will under-provision.
No TP sharding caveat: with TP greater than the KV head count, KV is replicated and per-GPU memory does not scale down.
